headline: A research firm says ASML is building a machine for hybrid bonding, a chip-stacking process, and shares in its Dutch rival Besi fell almost 3 percent.
score_reason: Kept at pool score: a research firm's inference that moved a listed company's shares on 16 Oct, with no ASML confirmation.
importance_line: It matters to Besi's investors and to chipmakers such as TSMC and Intel that buy bonding tools, because ASML would enter a market Besi now leads, but the claim rests on patent filings and the firm's own judgement, not an ASML statement.
summary: The research firm SemiAnalysis reports, as relayed by Investing.com on Yahoo Finance, that ASML, the Dutch maker of chip-printing machines, is developing a tool for die-to-wafer hybrid bonding, an advanced way of stacking chips onto wafers, judging by 27 patent families it filed between December 2022 and November 2024; ASML has announced nothing. Shares in Besi, the Dutch equipment maker that is the only supplier with such tools in volume production, fell nearly 3 percent on Friday 16 Oct 2026, and SemiAnalysis expects advanced logic chips, where Besi's business is concentrated at TSMC and Intel, to adopt ASML's tool first.
notes: Pool source SCMP (HTTP 403) not opened; read SemiAnalysis's public page and Investing.com on Yahoo Finance (finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/besi-shares-slide-report-asml-123139833.html). SCMP's angle on Chinese firms adopting hybrid bonding is not confirmed by any readable source. SemiAnalysis published on 15 Oct 2026 (evening GMT); the share move and coverage are 16 Oct.
